title: Part 3 Practice: Business Cycle and Macroeconomic Problems

options: A) Daily fluctuations in stock prices
B) Alternating periods of economic expansion and contraction
questions.correct_answer: B) Alternating periods of economic expansion and contraction
questions.explanation: The BUSINESS CYCLE is the natural rhythm of the economy: EXPANSION (growing GDP) followed by CONTRACTION (falling GDP). Phases: Expansion → Peak → Recession → Trough → Recovery. This cycle repeats over years.

questions.text: A RECESSION is technically defined as:
options: A) One quarter of negative growth
B) Two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
C) Any period of high inflation
D) Rising unemployment for one month
questions.correct_answer: B) Two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
questions.explanation: A RECESSION is officially defined as TWO CONSECUTIVE QUARTERS (6 months) of NEGATIVE GDP growth. A DEPRESSION is a severe, prolonged recession (like the 1930s). Recessions mean falling output and rising unemployment.
Unemployment Rate = (Unemployed / Labor Force) × 100. The LABOR FORCE = Employed + Unemployed (actively seeking work). People not looking for work (students, retirees) are NOT in the labor force.

questions.text: A recent graduate who is SEARCHING for their first job is:
questions.explanation: FRICTIONAL unemployment is the temporary unemployment during JOB SEARCH — graduates looking for first jobs, workers between jobs. It's natural and even healthy (allows matching workers to best jobs).

questions.text: When technology replaces workers (e.g., ATMs replacing bank tellers), this is:
questions.explanation: STRUCTURAL unemployment occurs when workers' SKILLS don't match available jobs. Technology changes (ATMs, automation) eliminate some jobs while creating others requiring different skills. Workers need retraining.

questions.text: Unemployment caused by an economic RECESSION is:
questions.explanation: CYCLICAL unemployment results from economic downturns. During recessions, firms lay off workers because demand falls. When the economy recovers, these workers are rehired. It's the most concerning type for policymakers.

options: B) Aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply
questions.correct_answer: B) Aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply
questions.explanation: DEMAND-PULL inflation happens when TOTAL DEMAND exceeds TOTAL SUPPLY — 'too much money chasing too few goods.' Consumers, businesses, and government all want more than the economy can produce, pulling prices UP.
TRADE DEFICIT = Imports > Exports (buying more from abroad than selling). BUDGET DEFICIT = Government spending > Tax revenue. Both are common problems in developing countries like Ethiopia.

options: B) Rising production costs (e.g., oil prices)
questions.correct_answer: B) Rising production costs (e.g., oil prices)
questions.explanation: COST-PUSH inflation occurs when production COSTS rise (oil, wages, raw materials), forcing producers to charge higher prices. Example: Oil price increase raises transport costs, pushing up prices of all transported goods.

questions.text: If Labor Force = 50 million and Unemployed = 5 million, the unemployment rate is:
questions.explanation: Unemployment Rate = (5 / 50) × 100 = 10%. This means 10% of the labor force is actively seeking work but can't find it. The remaining 90% (45 million) are employed.
